overview.heading: What is B.Arch?
paragraphs: B.Arch is a five-year undergraduate degree for students who want to design buildings and other parts of the built environment. It mixes creative work with technical study, so students learn to turn ideas into plans, sections, models, and drawings that can be built in real life. The course usually involves studio work, assignments, site understanding, and regular critiques.

A student in B.Arch spends a lot of time drawing, making models, using design software, and thinking about how people will use spaces. The work is not only about how a building looks. It also covers structure, function, climate, materials, and how a design fits into a city or neighbourhood. That is why the course suits people who enjoy both art and problem-solving.

In India, a B.Arch degree leads toward the profession of architect, but graduation alone is not the final step for legal practice. A person must register with the Council of Architecture to use the title Architect and practise the profession, and that registration needs renewal. For families, the course makes sense when the student wants a design career that combines creativity, discipline, and long-term technical learning.

curriculum.assessment_methods: Studio juries, design reviews, written exams, portfolio submission, model and drawing assessments, site study reports, and final thesis review are common in B.Arch programmes in India.
curriculum.learning_activities: Students usually spend time in design studios, drawing and drafting classes, model making, site visits, measurement exercises, computer-aided design work, group presentations, and internship or practical training linked to professional practice.

parent_corner.intro: B.Arch suits students who like drawing, design, and thinking about how buildings shape daily life. In India, it is a 5-year undergraduate degree, and the field is regulated by the Council of Architecture under the Architects Act, 1972. Families should separate two steps: earning the degree and qualifying to practise. A student can complete B.Arch, but to use the title architect and work professionally, registration with the Council of Architecture is required. That makes the course both creative and regulated. The work style is studio-heavy, so steady effort matters more than last-minute study. Parents can help by checking whether the student enjoys sketching, model-making, careful observation, and long projects, not only exams. It also helps to confirm the admission rules of each college early, because institutions may differ in entry requirements.
